packing: • Two climates: waterproof shell, warm mid-layer and grippy shoes for Iceland; sun shirts, hats and light clothes for Campania.
• Water kit: two swimsuits each, compact towels, water shoes, reef-safe sunscreen and motion-sickness plan for hydrofoils/boats.
• Sleep: blackout masks for Iceland’s bright nights and a compact fan only if lodging lacks strong AC.
• Driving: US licenses plus IDPs, two automatic confirmations and offline maps.

itinerary.labelHtml:
Day by Day

The canonical 12-night itinerary

Every activity has a current price/status, climate reality, picky-eater fallback and weather alternative.

days.heading: Pittsburgh → Keflavík

facts.label: Flight
facts.valueHtml: Seasonal PIT–KEF proxy; exact 2027 operation required

days.note: Book PIT→FCO on Icelandair with a four-night Iceland stopover if the Jun 10 nonstop and Jun 15 KEF→FCO connection price together correctly.

days.heading: Land in Iceland + geothermal reset
days.note: Keep the first day deliberately light.

spots.name: Reykjavík arrival + Laugardalslaug
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · reykjavikIG · laugardalslaugFlickr

images.alt: Reykjavík skyline glowing beneath a dramatic summer sunset
images.credit: Hallgrimur P. Helgason · Google Images source

images.alt: The Sun Voyager sculpture silhouetted against Reykjavík's golden waterfront
Harpa concert hall reflected in Reykjavík harbor at blue hour
Hallgrímskirkja rising above Reykjavík in a long-exposure night view
Hallgrímskirkja and Reykjavík rooftops under saturated sunset light

spots.cost: Laugardalslaug’s city prices remain the value play; the official pool specification lists a 28°C / 82°F main pool, 29°C / 84°F children’s pool, 32°C / 90°F wading pool and 38–44°C / 100–111°F hot tubs. Budget about $90–140 for airport transfer or first rental day, pool admission, groceries and dinner.
spots.climate: June air is commonly in the low-to-upper 50s°F; the water is reliably warm. This is deliberately not an ocean-swim day. Keep the first afternoon outside, eat early and use the pool to reset after the overnight flight.
spots.saveHtml: Save Use the municipal pool instead of a premium lagoon and buy breakfast/trail food at Bónus or Krónan.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A central apartment with breakfast space and blackout curtains is worth more than an arrival-day tour.
spots.restoHtml:
• Eldsmiðjan — wood-fired pizza and plain toppings
  • Hamborgarafabrikkan — burgers and fries
  • Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur — fast hot-dog fallback downtown
spots.altboxHtml:
• Flight delay: pool, groceries and sleep only.
  • Rain: Hallgrímskirkja, Harpa and the pool remain easy.
spots.spotMapHtml: 📍 Open in Google Maps ↩

days.heading: Golden Circle + Secret Lagoon
days.note: One classic circuit and one paid soak.

spots.name: Golden Circle + Secret Lagoon
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · goldencircleIG · gullfossIG · secretlagoonFlickr

images.alt: Gullfoss thundering through its rugged canyon under summer sky
The green rift valley and clear water of Þingvellir National Park
Strokkur geyser erupting high into a textured Icelandic sky
Silky turquoise water cascading over volcanic shelves near Gullfoss
A rainbow arcing through the spray above Gullfoss

spots.cost: Þingvellir, Geysir and Gullfoss have no attraction admission; budget parking and food. Secret Lagoon’s current planning proxy is about 3,000 ISK per adult with children 14 and under free, roughly $45–55 for this family before towels.
spots.climate: Plan around 45–58°F, wind and showers. The waterfall and rift walks are exposed, while the lagoon stays around 38–40°C / 100–104°F. Waterproof layers belong in the car even under a blue morning sky.
spots.saveHtml: Save Self-drive the classic loop and bring towels and a picnic.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Choose one paid experience only: Secret Lagoon is the warm-water anchor and the better family value.
spots.restoHtml:
• Efstidalur II — farm burgers, fries and ice cream
  • Mika — pizza and approachable plates near Reykholt
  • Friðheimar — tomato soup and bread if the greenhouse experience appeals
spots.altboxHtml:
• High wind: shorten Þingvellir and protect the lagoon reservation.
  • Late start: keep Gullfoss and Geysir; skip minor stops.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Secret Lagoon · official

days.heading: South Coast greatest hits
days.note: Long day, but the late light protects the pacing.

spots.name: South Coast: Seljalandsfoss, Skógafoss + Reynisfjara
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · skogafossIG · reynisfjaraIG · southcoasticelandFlickr

images.alt: Reynisfjara's black sand and basalt sea stacks in vivid evening light
Reynisdrangar sea stacks rising from the North Atlantic off Vík
Seljalandsfoss seen from the cavern path behind the waterfall
images.credit: Iceland Photo Tours · Google Images source

images.alt: Seljalandsfoss glowing gold in the midnight-sun season
images.credit: Iceland Photo Tours · Google Images source

images.alt: A rainbow forming in the mist below mighty Skógafoss

spots.cost: The waterfalls and black beach are free; allow roughly $100–160 for fuel, parking, food and a warm café stop. This is a long 10–12 hour Reykjavík day, so no glacier tour is stacked onto it.
spots.climate: Cold spray, wind and rapidly changing visibility. SafeTravel’s Reynisfjara warning system controls how close the family gets to the water; the beach is for scenery, never swimming.
spots.saveHtml: Save Pack lunch and use the late June light to spread the drive.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Pay for a comfortable automatic rental and full wind/gravel cover, not another tour.
spots.restoHtml:
• Black Crust Pizzeria — pizza in Vík
  • Smiðjan Brugghús — burgers and fries
  • The Soup Company — soup, bread and simple warm food
spots.altboxHtml:
• Red beach warning: view from the signed safe zone or skip Reynisfjara.
  • Severe weather: turn around after Seljalandsfoss; never force the full loop.

days.heading: Reykjanes weather-flex day

facts.label: Rule
facts.valueHtml: Use for a missed major loop if weather intervened

days.note: The fourth night earns its keep as weather insurance; Reykjanes is the lower-mileage plan only when the two flagship loops already succeeded.

spots.name: Reykjanes Peninsula + optional Blue Lagoon
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · reykjanesIG · gunnuhverIG · bluelagoonFlickr

images.alt: A powerful white steam plume rising from Gunnuhver's rust-colored geothermal field
A boardwalk leading through the steaming Gunnuhver geothermal landscape
Steam drifting across black lava and mineral earth on the Reykjanes Peninsula
Milky-blue geothermal water surrounded by dark volcanic rock at Blue Lagoon
A footbridge crossing Blue Lagoon's mineral-blue water beneath a fiery Icelandic sunset

spots.cost: Gunnuhver and the Reykjanes viewpoints are free. Keep Blue Lagoon optional until its 2027 rate and volcanic-access status are verified; a premium-lagoon family visit can add several hundred dollars, while a Reykjavík municipal pool keeps the flex day near $100–170 for fuel, food and swimming.
spots.climate: Use this day for whichever Iceland loop has the better forecast. If Golden Circle and South Coast both ran well, keep the lower-mileage Reykjanes circuit. Expect exposed wind, geothermal steam and cool air even beside hot water.
spots.saveHtml: Save Drive Gunnuhver and the Reykjanes coast, then repeat a municipal pool instead of buying Blue Lagoon admission.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Use Blue Lagoon only as the optional fourth-day splurge, with a cancellable booking and current volcanic-access check.
spots.restoHtml:
• Grindavík café or bakery — sandwiches and simple hot food when access permits
  • Keflavík pizzeria — plain pizza on the return toward Reykjavík
  • Reykjavík apartment dinner — grocery fallback after the loop
spots.altboxHtml:
• South Coast weather recovery: use this day for the missed waterfall loop instead.
  • Volcanic closure: skip the peninsula and keep Reykjavík, Perlan and a municipal pool.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Blue Lagoon · officialSafeTravel · official

days.heading: KEF → FCO → Naples → Ischia

facts.label: Ferry
facts.valueHtml: Alilauro 2026 summer proxy: frequent daily departures

days.note: This is the route’s most complex day. Use a generous flight-to-train-to-ferry buffer and keep the final hydrofoil cancellable.

days.heading: Castello Aragonese + Forio sunset
days.feel: Castle, first warm swim, white church
days.note: The beach follows the castle climb; Forio and Soccorso supply the sunset without needing a separate island day.

spots.name: Castello Aragonese + Ischia Ponte swim
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · castelloaragoneseIG · ischiapontFlickr

images.alt: Castello Aragonese poised above the blue water off Ischia Ponte
Castello Aragonese and Ischia Ponte settling into pastel dusk
The castle island framed by open Tyrrhenian water and luminous clouds
Castello Aragonese mirrored in calm water at sunset
A full moon rising behind the stone walls of Castello Aragonese

spots.cost: Carry about €45–60 for family castle admission until the 2027 tariff is posted, plus €20–35 for buses and beach logistics. The climb has steps and steep sections; go at opening, then swim below Ischia Ponte.
spots.climate: Typical mid-June air reaches the upper 70s to low 80s°F; planning sea temperature is about 74–76°F. The Tyrrhenian swim is the warm-water requirement the route was built around.
spots.saveHtml: Save Use the island bus and the public beach after the castle.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A water taxi or sunset boat view of the castle earns more than a private guide for this family.
spots.restoHtml:
• Pizzeria Da Ciccio — pizza and pasta near Ischia Ponte
  • La Virgola — zingara toasted sandwiches and casual food
  • Ristorante Pizzeria Aglio Olio e Pomodoro — familiar pasta and pizza
spots.altboxHtml:
• Heat: castle at opening, long swim after lunch.
  • Low energy: photograph the castle from the bridge and keep the beach.
spots.spotMapHtml: 📍 Open in Google Maps ↩

spots.name: La Mortella + Forio sunset coast
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · forioischiaIG · lamortellaIG · chiesadelsoccorsoFlickr

images.alt: Forio harbor curving beneath Monte Epomeo at sunset
The white Chiesa del Soccorso silhouetted against a Forio sunset
Forio's colorful waterfront and fishing boats beneath a deep blue sky
A broad view over Forio and Ischia's brilliant western shoreline
A palm framing the sun as it drops into the sea west of Forio

spots.cost: La Mortella’s official 2026 prices are €15 adult, €10 ages 12–18 and €8 ages 6–11: €48 for this family. The garden currently opens Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday; build the day around the actual 2027 opening calendar.
spots.climate: Warm, dry and bright, with sunset after 8:30pm. Use the shaded garden in the hottest hours, then Chiaia beach and Chiesa del Soccorso for golden hour.
spots.saveHtml: Save Walk Forio’s lanes and Soccorso viewpoint for free; use a public section of Chiaia beach.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A small-group island boat is the alternative splurge if conditions are calm.
spots.restoHtml:
• La Tinaia — wood-fired pizza and handmade pasta
  • La Casereccia — Margherita pizza and grilled fish/meat
  • Forio gelateria — easy sunset dessert
spots.altboxHtml:
• Garden closed: boat circuit or extra San Montano swim.
  • Rough sea: La Mortella, Forio lanes and sunset remain intact.
spots.spotMapHtml: 📍 Open in Google Maps ↩

days.heading: San Montano + Negombo
days.note: Confirm the 8-year-old’s height against thermal-pool restrictions before buying.

spots.name: San Montano Bay + Negombo thermal park
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · negomboischiaIG · sanmontanoFlickr

images.alt: A sculpted thermal pool opening toward the sea at Negombo
Terraced thermal water overlooking San Montano Bay
Crystal-clear blue water along Ischia's sheltered northwest coast
San Montano's crescent bay wrapped in green headlands
A quiet mineral pool carved among volcanic rock and subtropical plants

spots.cost: Negombo’s official 2026 shoulder-season list charges €55 one adult, €100 for two adults and €28 for a child 1.0–1.4m; taller children pay adult price. A realistic family gate is €128–160 ($145–180), with some thermal pools restricted for children under 1.4m. San Montano’s sea remains the guaranteed family swim.
spots.climate: Warm shallow bay plus temperature-varied pools. Mid-June sea planning range is 74–76°F; thermal water is warmer. Confirm the 8-year-old’s height against each pool restriction before paying.
spots.saveHtml: Save Use free San Montano beach and buy only a late-day Negombo entry if the pool rules fit.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge The full-day thermal park is the marquee Ischia splurge, but only after confirming child access.
spots.restoHtml:
• La Tinaia — pizza and handmade pasta in Forio
  • La Casereccia — broad pizza menu and grilled dishes
  • Forio bakery/panini counter — beach picnic fallback
spots.altboxHtml:
• Child-height mismatch: skip the park and stay at San Montano.
  • Cloudy day: thermal park still works; protect sun breaks for the bay.
spots.spotMapHtml: 📍 Open in Google Maps ↩

days.heading: Ischia → Naples → Santa Maria di Castellabate
days.note: Collect the mainland automatic only after the ferry; do not bring a car onto Ischia.

days.heading: Castellabate + Punta Licosa
days.note: A genuine beach day with a hill-town sunset.

spots.name: Santa Maria di Castellabate + Punta Licosa
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · castellabateIG · puntalicosaIG · cilentoFlickr

images.alt: Wind-shaped pines leaning over Punta Licosa's protected coastline
Punta Licosa's low lighthouse island surrounded by glowing shallow water
The sun setting over the calm protected water at Punta Licosa
The white Licosa lighthouse standing beyond the surf
Pine silhouettes and luminous water at Punta Licosa twilight

spots.cost: Public beaches and Punta Licosa access are free. Budget €25–45 for parking/local transport and €35–60 for loungers only if desired. The official local guide identifies Lago’s white sand, clear shallows, equipped beaches and children’s facilities as the family-fit stretch.
spots.climate: Late-June air commonly reaches the low-to-mid 80s°F and the sea about 75–77°F. Mornings are calmest; keep the hottest afternoon flexible between shade, apartment and water.
spots.saveHtml: Save Choose a walkable apartment near the beach and use public sand.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A short licensed boat to Licosa or the marine reserve gives the coast-scale reveal without a full private day.
spots.restoHtml:
• Castello dell’Abate restaurant/pizzeria — pizza options and a broad menu
  • Il Calesse — pizza and familiar Cilento plates
  • Beachfront lido café — fries, panini and simple pasta
spots.altboxHtml:
• Wind: use the most sheltered local cove and make Castellabate old town the afternoon.
  • Low energy: repeat the closest sand instead of chasing beaches.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Santa Maria di Castellabate · Visit Cilento
spots.spotMapHtml: 📍 Open in Google Maps ↩

days.heading: Paestum at opening + beach
days.note: The temples get the cool morning; the sea gets the afternoon.

spots.name: Paestum temples + family beach
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · paestumIG · templeofneptuneFlickr

images.alt: The Temple of Neptune at Paestum glowing at sunset
A rhythmic line of ancient Doric columns at Paestum
Paestum's Temple of Neptune illuminated beneath a blue night sky
Warm sunlight piercing the monumental stone doorway of a Paestum temple
images.credit: Magna Graecia Paestum · Google Images source

images.alt: Paestum's Greek temple framed by umbrella pines and bright spring sky
images.credit: Magna Graecia Paestum · Google Images source

spots.cost: The official 2026 March–November ticket is €15 per adult and free under 18, so €30 for the family. It includes Paestum, Velia and the Paestum museum for three consecutive days; booking is not mandatory. Add €20–35 for parking/fuel and use a public beach afterward.
spots.climate: Open archaeological plain, little shade, then warm sea. Enter at 8:30am, finish before peak heat and make the beach the second half of the day.
spots.saveHtml: Save Children are free; skip a private guide and use the official app/museum.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A buffalo-mozzarella farm lunch is the culturally relevant upgrade.
spots.restoHtml:
• Caseificio Barlotti — mozzarella, pasta and simple farm plates
  • Paestum pizzeria — Margherita and fries
  • Santa Maria apartment dinner — grocery fallback after the drive
spots.altboxHtml:
• Extreme heat: site at opening, museum, then pool/beach.
  • Rain: museum first and shorten the outdoor circuit.
spots.spotMapHtml: 📍 Open in Google Maps ↩

days.heading: Palinuro caves + final big swim
days.note: Run only with a good sea-state forecast and a real cancellation policy.

spots.name: Capo Palinuro sea caves + Natural Arch
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · palinuroIG · grottaazzurraIG · cilentocoastFlickr

images.alt: Capo Palinuro's steep limestone cliffs dropping into intense blue water
A sheltered blue cove cut into the rocky coast of Capo Palinuro
Capo Palinuro's sculpted rock wall viewed from the sea
A small boat floating in a secluded turquoise Palinuro cove
A luminous sunset spreading across the Tyrrhenian Sea off Palinuro

spots.cost: Current operator pages publish the route and timing but not a stable 2027 family tariff. Carry a planning allowance of €120–180 ($135–205) for a licensed family boat, parking and fees; mark the exact quote unknown until the operator calendar opens.
spots.climate: Warm water around 75–77°F, but cave access depends on swell. Take the first safe departure and preserve a beach alternative; never pay a nonrefundable rate without a weather policy.
spots.saveHtml: Save Choose a shared motorboat rather than private charter and pack lunch.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A longer shared coast circuit that enters the Blue Grotto and reaches hidden coves is the right splurge.
spots.restoHtml:
• Marì Pizza-Bistrot — pizza and hamburgers
  • La Taverna del Porto — pizza directly by the port beach
  • Aria di Mare — Neapolitan pizza and handmade pasta
spots.altboxHtml:
• Rough sea: Natural Arch viewpoint and a sheltered beach.
  • Long-drive fatigue: replace Palinuro with a second Licosa/Castellabate water day.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Capo Palinuro boat route
spots.spotMapHtml: 📍 Open in Google Maps ↩

days.heading: Cilento → Fiumicino buffer
days.feel: Drive north, return car, choose the evening by arrival time

facts.label: If parked by 3pm
facts.valueHtml: Leonardo Express to Rome: 32 min nonstop

days.note: The airport night remains insurance, but it need not be dead time. If the car is returned and bags are stored by about 3pm, take the €40 mini-group Leonardo Express for a compact Trevi–Pantheon–Piazza Navona evening. If arrival slips, walk Borgo Valadier and the Fiumicino canal waterfront. Ostia Antica is only viable with a much earlier arrival because June last entry is 6pm.

spots.name: Rome evening or Fiumicino waterfront
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · romeIG · trevifountainIG · piazzanavonaIG · fiumicinoFlickr

images.alt: Trevi Fountain glowing above turquoise water after dark in Rome
Piazza Navona opening beneath a luminous blue-hour sky
Castel Sant'Angelo and its bridge reflected across the Tiber at blue hour
St. Peter's Basilica and the Tiber glowing beneath a saturated Roman sunset
Fishing boats lining Fiumicino's canal waterfront beneath a warm sunset
images.credit: Porti di Roma · Google Images source

spots.cost: If the car is returned and bags are stored by about 3pm, Trenitalia’s current Leonardo Express family mini-group fare is €40 for up to four people each way. Keep the Rome walk compact and free apart from food; if arrival is later, the Fiumicino canal waterfront and Borgo Valadier walk cost nothing.
spots.climate: Rome is the reward only when the buffer remains comfortable. Use Trevi → Pantheon → Piazza Navona when parked by about 3pm. If the Cilento drive slips, stay local for the canal at sunset rather than turning the insurance night into another hard transfer.
spots.saveHtml: Save Choose the free Fiumicino waterfront walk and an early seafood or pizza dinner.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Take the Leonardo Express for a compact Rome evening, but skip taxis and timed attractions so the return stays flexible.
spots.restoHtml:
• Rome historic center pizzeria — plain pizza or pasta along the walking loop
  • Fiumicino canal pizzeria — easy late-arrival fallback
  • Airport-hotel dinner — the no-stress option if traffic consumes the evening
spots.altboxHtml:
• Parked by 3pm: train to Rome for Trevi, Pantheon and Piazza Navona.
  • Later arrival: Borgo Valadier and the Fiumicino canal waterfront at sunset.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Leonardo Express · officialBorgo Valadier · official

days.heading: FCO → Pittsburgh
days.note: Reject any itinerary that arrives June 24.

preDepartureTodos.labelHtml:
Pre-Departure To-Do

What to solve before leaving

The flight construction is the gate; activities come later.

blocks.when: As soon as exact flights price
blocks.title: Route and beds
items: Quote PIT→FCO with a four-night Iceland stopover and a protected FCO→PIT Jun 23 return.
Hold four refundable lodging bases and both automatic cars.
Reject any routing that arrives Pittsburgh June 24.

blocks.title: Transport and timed anchors
items: Confirm hydrofoil schedules, baggage rules and a wide Jun 15 buffer.
Recheck Negombo child-height restrictions and reserve the protected warm-water day.
Select licensed Ischia/Cilento boats with written weather cancellation terms.

blocks.title: Conditions
items: Check SafeTravel, Iceland road/weather and Reynisfjara warning level daily.
Check Campania marine forecasts and move boat days before cancellation windows.
Download offline maps, rail/hydrofoil tickets and restaurant fallbacks.

preDepartureTodos.callout: Non-negotiable: the second leg remains a warm-water beach trip. If the Italy sea/route fails, replace the second leg—do not substitute a cool Atlantic beach.
